newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end slightly up in narrow trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end slightly up in narrow trade.

text.p: The Taiwan stock index fluctuated narrowly to end slightly higher on Thursday and brokers said they expected share prices to move around current levels in coming sessions.
The weighted index, seesawing in a 56-point range, finished 22.88 points higher at 6,825.62. Turnover was T$43 billion.
Big-capital shares and blue chips attracted most buying.

"It's safer to buy big-capital shares when the market is not especially bullish," said Allen Huang, a manager at National Securities. "Investors feel confident about their operations when the economy starts picking up."
Taiwan's economy has begun a slow recovery in the fourth quarter and many analysts expect further recovery in 1997.

Stocks related to the influential conglomerate Formosa Plastics group led the gains, with Formosa Chemical Fibres up T$1.6 or 3.85 percent to T$43.2 and Formosa Plastics gaining T$2.5 or 3.7 percent to T$70. Another key Formosa member, Nan Ya, rose T$2 or 3.15 percent at T$65.5.
Some brokers noted minor buying by government funds to support overall market sentiment, but concurred that they did not seem to be trying to trigger a rally as seen in November.
Moody's announcement of strong Aa3 long-term and Prime-1 short-term ratings for the International Commercial Bank of China had little impact on the sluggish market, brokers said.

Moody's also assigned a C-Plus financial strength rating to reflect good financial fundamentals the bank, one of Taiwan's oldest and biggest private banks. Its share price edged up only 50 cents or 0.6 percent to T$84.5.
"Big-capital shares and blue chips will rise in turns but I don't see major movements," said Taiwan Securities' Joe Chiou.
A 6,750-6,850 trading range was seen in the near term.
